email.subject1: a signal play for Blue Ridge
email.body1:
Nicole, saw Blue Ridge launched Blu, your GenAI Forecasting Companion, this past October.

A net-new AI launch usually opens more in-market accounts than enablement and BD can personally touch before the category moment fades. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Blue Ridge off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Nicole, quick follow-up for Blue Ridge.

With Blu in market, demand often outpaces what the BD team can cover. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book to capitalize on a launch, so the gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Blue Ridge needs to ride the Blu launch, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Nicole, last bit of proof for Blue Ridge.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Blue Ridge's reply rate likely compares to other supply-chain software teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Nicole, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority while Blu rolls out, no problem at all. Timing is everything around a product launch, and that stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to an enablement-led motion? I'll tailor it to Blue Ridge either way.
